summary: Strip cutoff depends on scaling matrix and leaves an admissible geodesic wholly untruncated, invalidating literal regularisation used in the continuous-spectrum proof. Main conclusions not disproved.

problems.decisive_evidence: Both inverse-scaled real parts0, so no endpoint removed for anyY. Upper-end antiderivative i(B^s+phi B^(1-s)) has unbounded subsequence for s=.5+i. Scaling I vsT gives distinct strips.

problems.impact: Central regularized integral undefined literally; proof bridge fails as written. No main-theorem counterexample.
problems.counterevidence: Full-horoball correction yields paired finite cutoff; in example integral identically0 by modular symmetry.
problems.correction: Remove real-part restriction or explicitly use full preimage of quotient cusp neighborhoods; recheck scaling5.10, all-endpoint cancellation, Stokes boundaries.

scientific_checks.hypotheses: An arbitrary geodesic in H with two distinct rational endpoints is allowed. The imaginary axis has endpoints infinity and zero; I and S are allowed scaling matrices; t=1 is an allowed real spectral parameter.
scientific_checks.independent_derivation: For z=iy both inverse-scaled real parts equal zero, so the strict 0<Re<1 zones remove no point for any Y. The original source image confirms the strict inequalities and that the sets are in H. The even Fourier expansion makes partial_x E vanish on the axis; integrating R0 E dz/Im z gives i(E(iB,s)-E(iA,s)). At s=1/2+i choose theta with exp(i theta)+phi(s)exp(-i theta) nonzero; B_n=exp(theta+2pi n) gives an unbounded leading term of modulus proportional to sqrt(B_n). No numerical approximation is used.
scientific_checks.counterevidence: Full horoballs restore scaling independence. On the same example the remaining segment i/Y to iY has integral zero by modular inversion. A quotient interpretation requires complete lifts; it is not the defined strip cutoff. This does not prove that intended regularization or equidistribution is impossible.
scientific_checks.actual_dependency: Lemma5.4 and Corollary5.5 supply the regularized periods explicitly used by Lemma6.10 on PDF53-54. Its Stokes proof uses the same cusp zones; this is a central continuous-spectrum proof dependency.
scientific_checks.severity_and_repair: Major reflects the literal undefined integral and invalid stated proof input. Ease of modifying the cutoff does not reduce severity. General horoball scaling, cancellation and Stokes multiplicities remain to be verified together.

independent_acceptance_review.unconfirmed_candidates: The missing inverse eigenvalue in later topological terms and the noninjective-ball interpretation remain unresolved, with no admissible decisive counterexample. Neither is promoted to a confirmed Problem.
